turn_text: Nebraska Congressman Don Bacon joined 21 other House Republicans Wednesday and not voting for Jim Jordan as Speaker of the House. Nebraska Public Media's Brian Beach heard from Bacon about why he voted the way he did. Bacon voted for former Speaker Kevin McCarthy in two House elections this week and called out the eight Republicans who ousted him earlier this month.

The fact is the eight people that did this three weeks ago, they were wrong for what they did to our country, to the House. to their own party, how they treated Kevin McCarthy and, and hopefully the voters there will take, will hold it responsible.

Bacon says Jim Jordan has done a good job as chair of the Judiciary Committee and has come a long way from when he was first elected. But Bacon says his lack of support for Jordan is about accountability for the group that broke Republican committee rules by bringing the speaker vote to the House floor without approval from a majority of Republicans. What
point do you say? Okay, I got to follow the rules and they can't. I wanted accountability. And I want consequences for what happened.
Bacon says he believes the house could elect a speaker quickly if Jordan withdraws himself from the race. I'm Brian Beach, Nebraska Public Media News.
